sentences.zh: 河東道，蓋古冀州之域，漢河東、太原、上黨、西河、鴈門、代郡及鉅鹿、常山、趙國、廣平國之地。

translations.literal: The Hedong Circuit — broadly the territory of ancient Jizhou, comprising the Han commanderies of Hedong, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Yanmen, and Dai and the principalities of Julu, Changshan, Zhao, and Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong Circuit lay within the ancient Jizhou region, covering the Han commanderies of Hedong, Taiyuan, Shangdang, Xihe, Yanmen, and Dai together with the principalities of Julu, Changshan, Zhao, and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 河中、絳、晉、慈、隰、石、太原、汾、忻、潞、澤、沁、遼為實沈分，代、雲、朔、蔚、武、新、嵐、憲為大梁分。

translations.literal: There are two garrisons, namely Miyun and Baitan.
translations.idiomatic: It had two garrison commands: Miyun and Baitan.

translations.literal: There is the Qingyi Army, established in the Chuigong era.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Qingyi Army, established in the Chuigong era.

sentences.zh: 有淮北、白陽度、雲治、廣邊四鎮兵。

translations.literal: There are four garrison forces: Huaibei, Baiyangdu, Yunzhi, and Guangbian.
translations.idiomatic: It had four garrison forces: Huaibei, Baiyangdu, Yunzhi, and Guangbian.

translations.literal: There are two outposts: Henghe and Chaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: It had two outposts: Henghe and Chaicheng.
It had Yangmen City.

translations.literal: There are two passes: Yongding and Yaozi.
translations.idiomatic: It had two passes: Yongding and Yaozi.

sentences.zh: 又有懷柔軍，在媯、蔚二州之境。

translations.literal: There is also the Huairou Army, in the territory of Gui and Wei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Huairou Army, in the territory of Gui and Wei prefectures.
Huairou.
Upper rank.

sentences.zh: 天寶中析置媯川縣，尋省。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era Guichuan County was carved out and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Guichuan County was carved out and soon abolished.

translations.literal: The Gui River runs through its center.
translations.idiomatic: The Gui River ran through its center.

sentences.zh: 北九十里有長城，開元中張說築。

translations.literal: Ninety li north is the Great Wall, built by Zhang Yue in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety li to the north lay the Great Wall, built by Zhang Yue in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 東南五十里有居庸塞，東連盧龍、碣石，西屬太行、常山，實天下之險。

translations.literal: Fifty li southeast is Juyong Pass; east it connects with Lulong and Jieshi, west it belongs to the Taihang and Changshan ranges—it is truly the greatest strategic barrier under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li to the southeast lay Juyong Pass; eastward it connected with Lulong and Jieshi, westward with the Taihang and Changshan ranges—truly the greatest strategic barrier under Heaven.
It had Tiemen Pass.

translations.literal: To the west is the Ningwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: To its west lay the Ningwu Army.

sentences.zh: 又北有廣邊軍，故白雲城也。

translations.literal: Farther north is the Guangbian Army, the old Baiyun City.
translations.idiomatic: Farther north lay the Guangbian Army at the old Baiyun City.

sentences.zh: 檀州檀州密雲郡，本安樂郡，天寶元年更名。

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture, Tan Prefecture, Miyun Commandery; formerly Anle Commandery; renamed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Prefecture, Miyun Commandery designation; formerly Anle Commandery; renamed in the first year of Tianbao.
Its local tribute included ginseng and musk.

sentences.zh: 戶六千六十四，口三萬二百四十六。

translations.idiomatic: It had 6,064 households and a population of 30,246.
It administered two counties.
Miyun was middle rank.
It had Mount Kui.
Yanle.
Middle rank.

sentences.zh: 東北百八十五里有東軍、北口二守捉。

translations.literal: One hundred eighty-five li northeast are the Dongjun and Beikou frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred eighty-five li to the northeast lay the Dongjun and Beikou frontier garrisons.

translations.literal: Beikou is the Great Wall Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Beikou was the Great Wall Pass.

sentences.zh: 又北八百里有吐護真河，奚王衙帳也。

translations.literal: Eight hundred li farther north is the Tuhuzhen River, the seat of the Xi king.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred li farther north lay the Tuhuzhen River, the seat of the Xi king.

translations.literal: Ji Prefecture, Ji Prefecture, Yuyang Commandery, lower.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Prefecture, Yuyang Commandery designation, lower rank.

translations.literal: Established in the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan from You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan from You Prefecture.
Its local tribute included white glue.

sentences.zh: 戶五千三百一十七，口萬八千五百二十一。

translations.idiomatic: It had 5,317 households and a population of 18,521.
It administered three counties.
Yuyang, Sanhe, and Yutian.

sentences.zh: 營州營州柳城郡，上都督府。

translations.literal: Ying Prefecture, Ying Prefecture, Liucheng Commandery, upper military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture, Liucheng Commandery designation, upper military governorship.

sentences.zh: 本遼西郡，萬歲通天元年為契丹所陷，聖曆二年僑治漁陽，開元五年又還治柳城，天寶元年更名。

translations.literal: Formerly Liaoxi Commandery; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian it fell to the Khitan; in the second year of Shengli the seat was provisionally at Yuyang; in the fifth year of Kaiyuan it returned to Liucheng; renamed in the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Liaoxi Commandery; in the first year of Wansui Tongtian it fell to the Khitan; in the second year of Shengli the seat was provisionally at Yuyang; in the fifth year of Kaiyuan it returned to Liucheng; renamed in the first year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 土貢：人葠、麝香、豹尾、皮骨𩨸。

translations.literal: Local tribute: ginseng, musk, leopard tails, and hide-and-bone saddles.
translations.idiomatic: Its local tribute included ginseng, musk, leopard tails, and hide-and-bone saddles.

sentences.zh: 戶九百九十七，口三千七百八十九。

translations.idiomatic: It had 997 households and a population of 3,789.
It administered one county.
Liucheng.
Middle rank.

sentences.zh: 西北接奚，北接契丹，有東北鎮醫巫閭山祠。

translations.literal: To the northwest it borders the Xi; to the north the Khitan; there is the Northeast Garrison Shrine to Mount Yiwulü.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest it bordered the Xi; to the north the Khitan; it had the Northeast Garrison Shrine to Mount Yiwulü.
Farther east lay Mount Jieshi.

sentences.zh: 安東都護府安東，上都護府。

translations.idiomatic: The Andong Protectorate, upper protectorate.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，李勣平高麗國，得城百七十六，分其地為都督府九，州四十二，縣一百，置安東都護府於平壤城以統之，用其酋渠為都督、刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang, Li Ji subdued Goguryeo, taking one hundred seventy-six cities; the territory was divided into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and one hundred counties; the Andong Protectorate was established at Pyongyang to govern them, using their tribal chiefs as area commanders, prefects, and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongzhang, Li Ji subdued Goguryeo, taking one hundred seventy-six cities; the territory was divided into nine area commands, forty-two prefectures, and one hundred counties; the Andong Protectorate was established at Pyongyang to govern them, appointing their tribal chiefs as area commanders, prefects, and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 上元三年徙遼東郡故城，儀鳳二年又徙新城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan it was moved to the old Liaodong Commandery city; in the second year of Yifeng it was moved again to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shangyuan it was moved to the old Liaodong Commandery city; in the second year of Yifeng it was moved again to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 聖曆元年更名安東都督府，神龍元年復故名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengli it was renamed the Andong Area Command; in the first year of Shenlong it was restored to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengli it was renamed the Andong Area Command; in the first year of Shenlong it was restored to the former name.

sentences.zh: 開元二年徙于平州，天寶二年|743年又徙于遼西故郡城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan it was moved to Ping Prefecture; in the second year of Tianbao (743) it was moved again to the old Liaoxi commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan it was moved to Ping Prefecture; in the second year of Tianbao (743) it was moved again to the old Liaoxi commandery city.
It was abolished after the Zhide era.
Its local tribute included ginseng.

translations.literal: At right: the Hebei Surveillance Commissioner, seated at Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At right: the Hebei Surveillance Commissioner, with his seat at Wei Prefecture.
